summary.text: Case 1 is a 62-year-old female patient with no history of ocular or systemic disease who presented with bilateral blurred vision. Corrected distance visual acuity was 20/125 in the right eye and 20/63 in the left eye. Preoperative examination showed no corneal edema, and endothelial cell density was within the normal range.

General anesthesia was induced because of claustrophobia, and a preoperative antisepsis protocol using chlorhexidine gluconate with isopropanol, povidone-iodine and 83% alcohol was applied, without applying antisepsis to both eyes simultaneously. The right eye underwent uneventful surgery and was patched, after which the left eye was disinfected and draped separately.

Central corneal haziness was then noted, markedly more evident in the left eye per the figure caption; it worsened during continuous curvilinear capsulorhexis and gradually improved during cortex removal, allowing successful intraocular lens implantation, after which the left eye haziness had resolved. A dispersive viscosurgical device protected the endothelium and phacoemulsification used reduced ultrasound power. Postoperatively CDVA was 20/20 in both eyes, and specular microscopy and pachymetry remained stable at 3 months.

summary.text: Case 2 is a 61-year-old female patient who underwent immediately sequential bilateral cataract surgery under general anesthesia. As in case 1, the right eye was operated first, and nucleus removal in the right and left eyes is shown in the figure. Both patients had normal endothelial cell density.

After left eye disinfection and draping, central corneal haziness was observed, and the figure caption states it was markedly more evident in the left eye. The haze worsened during continuous curvilinear capsulorhexis and improved during cortex removal, allowing safe intraocular lens implantation, after which the left eye haziness had resolved; postoperative recovery was uneventful with corrected distance visual acuity of 20/20 in both eyes.
At 1 month, uncorrected visual acuity was 20/20 with a clear cornea on slitlamp examination, but the patient was lost to follow-up thereafter.

article_limitations: Caption-layer visual status is not_inspected; the actual JPEG is inspected in the separate visual target.
The authors' rabbit experiment (two New Zealand white rabbits) is an animal study, not a clinical case, and is not a roster patient; its facts are not annotated.

General statements about the two cases, such as no intraoperative trauma, OVD instability or anesthesia-related toxicity being evident, absent classic signs of epithelial disruption or hyperemia, and the antiseptic regimen including diluted chlorhexidine and 83% alcohol, do not explicitly name each patient and are not copied to individuals.
Case 1 antiseptic agents are recorded from the case 1 paragraph; the paragraph does not state which eye each preparation step applied to.
Supplementary Table 1 (PDF) holds patient-level endothelial and corneal thickness values; it is reviewed in the supplement sidecar, not as article segments.
Mechanistic statements about alcohol contact and toxicity are author hypotheses and are recorded only as ambiguities.

Supplementary Table 1 per-eye values (ECD, CV, HEX, CCT; case 1 before surgery and 3 months, case 2 before surgery, case 2 3 months NA) are recorded as typed facts in the supplement clinical sidecar, not as article-segment facts.
